content.text: {"headline":"Approve P4: evening overtime for 5 payments agents plus chat deflection lifts service level to 84.0% for 16:15-20:00 at ₹2,925.","why":"Both queues are short-staffed, mainly because agents are late due to the bus strike (payments 19 absences vs a usual 2.6, general 10 vs 2.4). Call volume is not the problem. With no action, payments drops to 69.4% and the overall service level to 75.9%, below the 80% target. P4 is the cheapest plan that meets the target. It cancels payments coaching 16:15-17:30, moves 3 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 17:00-18:00, deflects 20% of status and balance enquiries to chat on payments, adds overtime for 5 payments agents 18:00-20:00 and runs IVR callback on general 18:00-19:00. Predicted results: payments 82.8%, general 85.5%, abandon rate 4.0%. No policy issues and no escalation needed.","trade_offs":["P2 reaches 85.2% with the same 4.0% abandon rate, but costs ₹4,905, ₹1,980 more for about 1 point of service level.","P3 is the strongest option at 87.9% and 3.0% abandon rate, but costs ₹5,445, nearly double P4.","P1 costs only ₹225 but misses the target at 72.8%. It also pulls general down to 75.0%, so it is worse than doing nothing overall.","P4 has the thinnest margin on payments (82.8% vs 80% target), so it has the least room if things worsen."],"watch":"General handle time has been running 15% above forecast for the last two intervals. If that continues while 3 agents are on payments 17:00-18:00, general's margin could shrink. Check overtime uptake for the 18:00 start, and watch whether late agents arrive as the strike eases. If they do, some overtime may not be needed."}
